fact: Liberia's National Identification Registry says it is seeking about US$54.7 million to fund free national ID cards for disadvantaged citizens, to start once the agreement before the Legislature is ratified, and that county mapping for registration has begun.

The National Identification Registry says a proposed US$54.7 million investment by OeSD International for nationwide biometric enrolment and national identity infrastructure has reached the Legislature and awaits ratification.

Liberia has signed a $54 million agreement with OSD for a national identity infrastructure upgrade that still requires parliamentary approval, while national ID issuance has been suspended since June 2025.

NIR executive director Andrew Peters says the concession agreement with OeSD International for biometric enrolment, deduplication and digital and physical credentials is signed, but implementation awaits legislative rectification.

fact: The article says citizens outside Monrovia must travel to the capital to register and obtain national ID cards from the National Identification Registry, whose director says it wants to replace its current technology under a proposed US$39 million plan.
The NIR has concluded consultations on a concession agreement with OSD, now headed to Parliament, ahead of a nationwide biometric enrolment drive for a new national ID system.

Liberia's National Identification Registry said procurement of an Austrian firm to develop a new national biometric ID system under a public-private partnership is complete and a concession agreement finalised, awaiting presidential approval and legislative ratification.
The proclamation says about 720,000 people are enrolled in the NBIS and that every person in Liberia is required to enrol, with citizen or foreign-national status recorded.

The National Elections Commission handed over more than 500 biometric kits to the National Identification Registry to boost its enrolment capacity, and the NIR director said the kits still need licensing and technical modifications, following the NIR's May 2024 roadmap for comprehensive national enrollment.

The National Identification Registry, established in 2011 after the rollout of national biometric ID cards, registers citizens and non-citizens with a unique identification number, fingerprint data and photo.
The NIR enrols people into the National Biometric Identification System and had enrolled 740,000 by December 2024.
The Liberian Investigator reports that the NIR issues national ID cards at a US$5 fee and assigns unique identification numbers, as part of the government's national biometric identification system.
Techpoint Africa reports the National Identification Registry (NIR) issues unique ID cards to Liberians and has registration centres in every district and some townships.
